lessons.title: Planning across contexts
objectives: Select suitable A2.2 language for study, work, or community plans.
Use a main idea and one relevant detail in a response about planning across several situations.

content_sections.title: Notice form and meaning (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Read the model aloud twice: 'I can choose suitable future language for study, work, and community plans.' Underline the words that show the situation, time, or result. In this lesson, select suitable a2.2 language for study, work, or community plans. Keep the language connected: do not give isolated words.

content_sections.title: Guided dialogue (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Partner A begins a realistic exchange about planning across several situations. Partner B asks for one missing detail. Swap roles and make one change to the time, place, reason, quantity, or next action. Check that the exchange achieves: Select suitable A2.2 language for study, work, or community plans.

content_sections.title: Independent response (6 minutes)
content_sections.body: Create a short message about planning across several situations without reading the model. Include a main event or plan and one precise detail. Speak it once slowly, then once at a natural pace. Listen for whether the key information is clear.

exercises.prompt: Choose the response that gives a clear, useful message for this situation: planning across several situations.
options: I can choose suitable future language for study, work, and community plans.
My train arrived late, so I sent my friend a message before dinner.
I missed my connection, so I asked the station worker for another route.
exercises.correct_answer: I can choose suitable future language for study, work, and community plans.

exercises.prompt: Complete the model with the missing words: 'I can choose suitable future language for study, work, ____.'
Read this short message for the lesson 'Planning across contexts' and identify the real-life situation it describes.
exercises.stimulus: I can choose suitable future language for study, work, and community plans. The message gives one main point and one detail for the listener.

questions.question: What situation does the message describe?
acceptable_answers: The message is about planning across several situations.

exercises.prompt: Speak for 30–45 seconds about planning across several situations. State the main message, add a relevant detail, and answer one follow-up question.

criteria: Communicates the main message about planning across several situations clearly.
Adds a relevant detail and responds appropriately to a follow-up question.

listening.instruction: Listen once to a short message about planning across several situations. Answer the question before the transcript is revealed, then listen again and check the key detail.
listening.goal: Identify the situation and a useful detail in a short message about planning across several situations.
listening.transcript: I can choose suitable future language for study, work, and community plans.
listening.question: What is the message mainly about?
listening.answer: The listener should understand that it concerns planning across several situations.
constraints: Keep the transcript private before the learner answers the first question.
Use only the supplied transcript; do not require media.

speaking.instruction: Roleplay planning across several situations. Learner role: explain the situation and give one useful detail. Tutor role: be a helpful listener, ask one specific follow-up, and confirm the next step. Begin with a natural greeting and finish once both roles agree on the next action.
speaking.goal: Complete a clear, practical exchange about planning across several situations.
constraints: Name the learner and tutor roles before the first turn.
Use at most three tutor turns and stop after the agreed next step.

pronunciation.instruction: Say the model for planning across several situations in two thought groups. Mark the pause between ideas, then stress the word that gives the key action, time, quantity, reason, or request. Record a second attempt after listening to your first attempt.
pronunciation.goal: Make the key information in planning across several situations easy to hear.
pronunciation.target: Thought-group pause and key-word stress in planning across contexts
constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is supplied.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when learner audio is unavailable.

writing.instruction: Write a 35–50 word message about planning across several situations. Include the main event or plan, one precise detail, and the next action or response. Submit your own draft before requesting feedback.
writing.goal: Write a connected, useful short message about planning across several situations.
constraints: Wait for the learner draft before giving feedback.
Give concise feedback only; do not replace the learner draft.

lessons.title: Review: A2.2 consolidation
objectives: Review all A2.2 target dimensions before the unit test.
Use a main idea and one relevant detail in a response about reviewing A2.2 communication.

content_sections.title: Recall and select (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Work without notes first. For the situation 'reviewing A2.2 communication', say one sentence that meets this goal: Review all A2.2 target dimensions before the unit test. Then check the model: 'I can plan, invite, offer help, and explain a practical change clearly.' Identify one word or phrase that makes the message clear.

content_sections.title: Compare two responses (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Give one clear response for reviewing A2.2 communication, then ask a partner one follow-up question. Compare the response with the model and repair one missing time, reason, place, quantity, or next step. Use the whole unit's familiar language rather than memorising one sentence.

content_sections.title: Self-check and transfer (6 minutes)
content_sections.body: Before the unit test, check three things: the main message is clear, one useful detail is included, and the listener knows what happens next. Say or write a new short message about a similar situation, not the model about reviewing A2.2 communication.
